details: Living organisms exhibit all core life processes simultaneously.
Non-living objects may show an isolated feature (e.g., moving car, growing cloud) but lack internal metabolic cellular life processes.
experiments_or_examples: Comparing pigeon/snail (living) with pencil/car (non-living) in Table 10.1

details: Nutrition: Food provides energy for cellular maintenance and work.
Growth: Irreversible internal increase in body size and cell count.
Respiration: Biochemical breakdown of food in cells to release energy.
Response to Stimuli: Functional reaction to external changes (light, touch, temperature).
Excretion: Elimination of toxic metabolic waste products.
Reproduction: Producing new individual offspring of one's own species.
Lifespan: Finite cycle of birth, growth, maturation, aging, and death.
experiments_or_examples: Human breathing; animals eating food; plants growing towards sunlight

details: Chhui-mui (Touch-me-not / Mimosa pudica): Demonstrates rapid leaf folding and drooping when touched.
Latent Life in Seeds: Dry seeds in storage remain dormant with low metabolic rate; when supplied with water, air (oxygen), and warmth, they germinate into seedlings.
experiments_or_examples: Touching Chhui-mui leaves; germinating dry bean seeds on moist cotton
